items.title: John Altman interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 14, 2023
items.q: So for example an interesting one in terms of the pop music was Rod Stewart’s version of “Downtown Train,” the Tom Waits song, because we recorded it in the key of G

ctx.x: Yeah because then you’re running into like that doesn’t lie very well on this instrument now I’ve got to fuss with it.

Very true. Very true. And again, if I’m arranging a pop record for example, I’m always thinking of what the key is, what the vocalist is, and what can surround it in a certain way. So for example an interesting one in terms of the pop music was Rod Stewart’s version of “Downtown Train,” the Tom Waits song, because we recorded it in the key of G and then he found that his voice — because he’d abstained from smoking and worked out and whatever, it was too low. So they vari-sped it up to B flat. And this was the…
Wow. I have never heard of such a thing. And so it didn’t speed up the music.
